$comment: Pinned sources for the LGPL FFmpeg and ffprobe binaries PokitPlayer ships.
Replaces the ffmpeg-static / ffprobe-static npm packages, which downloaded GPL-3 builds (and, on macOS arm64, a build flagged --enable-nonfree that could not lawfully be redistributed at all).
Windows and Linux use BtbN's official LGPL variants - the '-lgpl' asset, not the default GPL one. Verified 2026-09-03: no --enable-gpl, no --enable-nonfree, and x264/x265/xvid explicitly disabled.
macOS has no published LGPL build from any reputable source (Homebrew, evermeet and osxexperts all ship GPL), so it is compiled from pinned FFmpeg source in CI by scripts/build-ffmpeg-macos.sh.
Every binary, however acquired, must pass scripts/verify-ffmpeg-license.js before it can be packaged. That gate - not this file - is the actual guarantee.

ON CHECKSUM DRIFT: BtbN publishes to a rolling 'latest' tag, so these hashes will eventually stop matching when upstream rebuilds. That is a deliberate fail-closed design: the fetch aborts rather than silently pulling an unreviewed binary. Re-pin with `npm run ffmpeg:fetch -- --update-checksums` after confirming the new build still passes the licence gate. For fully reproducible builds, mirror these artefacts to storage we control and set FFMPEG_MIRROR_BASE.

darwin-x64.$comment: Built natively on an x64 macOS runner. Do NOT cross-build from arm64 - the previous arrangement shipped an arm64 binary inside the Intel DMG, which could not execute at all on an Intel Mac.

darwin-arm64.$comment: Built natively on an arm64 macOS runner.

source.$comment: Used by the macOS build. The tarball SHA-256 is pinned for supply-chain integrity; it is separate from the licence guarantee, which comes from our own configure line plus the verify gate. If sha256 is null the build script prints the computed hash and fails, so a value is recorded deliberately rather than trusted blindly on first run.
